subject: Trade-secret confidentiality carve-out and evidence protocol — MSA redlines
messages:
From: Janelle Peters <janelle.peters@blueridgeanalytics.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueridgeanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-09-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines: carve-out for trade-secret confidentiality breaches

Ben —

Thanks for the conversation earlier. Our legal team reviewed the latest MSA and asked us to request a limited carve-out to the liability cap specifically tied to willful or negligent disclosure of trade secrets and highly sensitive confidential information. In practical terms, we are proposing:

- A narrow exception that would exclude proven trade-secret misappropriation from the overall liability cap;
- A companion evidentiary protocol (what counts as ‘trade secret’, who certifies it, timelines for notice and preservation) so this isn’t an open-ended exposure; and
- A mutual obligation to cooperate during an investigation (forensics, chain-of-custody).

I’ve attached a marked-up MSA that highlights the proposed language and a short summary of the evidence protocol we’d expect to rely on. Can you confirm Redwood’s ability to accept a limited cap carve-out on those terms, or suggest alternative wording that preserves commercial predictability?

Appreciate a quick read — Tom (procurement) is watching timelines.

Thanks,
Janelle Peters
Lead Counsel, Contracts
Blue Ridge Analytics

Attachments: BRA_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (redline), evidence_protocol_summary.pdf (summary)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Janelle Peters <janelle.peters@blueridgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueridgeanalytics.com>; marissa_cole@redwood.ai; rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-19T12:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: carve-out for trade-secret confidentiality breaches

Janelle —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. I’ve looped in Marissa (legal) and Rishi (contracts) so they can evaluate the specific proposed language and the evidence protocol.

Quick commercial note from my side: we understand the ask and want to keep the carve-out narrowly scoped. Broad or uncapped exposure materially changes the economics for this order form, so we’ll need precise definitions and a short, objective evidence path.

Marissa / Rishi — can you review the attached redline and the protocol and propose a version that balances BR’s need for recoverability in the event of trade-secret misappropriation with Redwood’s need for predictable caps/insurance alignment?

Goal: get to AGREE/FINAL redline within 3 business days if possible so procurement can finish approvals.

— Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai; Janelle Peters <janelle.peters@blueridgeanalytics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai; Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueridgeanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines: carve-out for trade-secret confidentiality breaches

Ben / Janelle / Team —

Thanks — I reviewed BRA_MSA_redlines_v3.docx and the evidence_protocol_summary. Below is Redwood’s proposed compromise language and the rationale. I’ve kept the carve-out narrowly tailored and added objective criteria to limit ambiguity. If BR agrees to this, we can insert it into the MSA and route for signature.

Proposed insertion (new subsection under Section 9: LIMITATION OF LIABILITY):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, the liability cap set forth in this Agreement shall not apply to damages arising from (i) proven willful or grossly negligent misappropriation of Customer trade secrets as defined under applicable law, provided that (ii) Customer provides written notice identifying (A) specific information alleged to be a trade secret, (B) the business value and measures taken to maintain secrecy, and (C) contemporaneous supporting evidence (forensic snapshot, access logs, or other verifiable records). Redwood’s aggregate liability for such trade-secret misappropriation shall be limited to direct damages proven in accordance with Section 10 (Indemnities), and in no event shall consequential, punitive or speculative damages be recoverable unless expressly required by applicable law."

Key points and limited evidence protocol we recommend including in a new Schedule X (attached as 'evidence_protocol_summary.pdf'):
- Definition: adopt the statutory definition of trade secret where available (state/federal), not a subjective label.
- Burden/timing: Customer must provide written notice within 30 days of discovery and preserve the relevant data/environment for a minimum of 90 days to allow for forensics.
- Third-party forensic: either party may appoint an independent forensic firm; costs are allocated to the prevailing party in a good-faith determination.
- Escrow/monetary cap fallback: if forensic results are inconclusive, both parties will proceed to mediation before either side may seek judicial remedies.

Why this protects both sides: BR preserves a recoverability path for demonstrable harms tied to trade-secret theft; Redwood avoids unlimited exposure and retains predictable limits for underwriting.

Please let me know if BR can accept this draft as a base. If Janelle is comfortable, I’ll prepare a tracked-change version for insertion.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Janelle Peters <janelle.peters@blueridgeanalytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueridgeanalytics.com>; rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-21T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: carve-out for trade-secret confidentiality breaches

Marissa —

Appreciate the thoughtful draft. A couple of small requests from our side:

1) Burden of proof — we’d like to make clear that the Customer need only demonstrate 'a preponderance of evidence' in the forensic report rather than a criminal standard; your draft reads like a civil standard but we want explicit clarity.
2) Preservation window — can BR ask for a 120-day hold instead of 90 given our internal compliance checkpoints?
3) Remedies — we prefer to preserve the possibility of injunctive relief outside the direct-damages route (for example, to stop an ongoing exfiltration). Can we add an express carve-in that equitable relief (injunctive/temporary restraining orders) remains available notwithstanding the damage-limitation provisions?

If you’re good with those, we’ll accept the proposed compromise and sign once the redline is updated.

Tom — we should confirm procurement can accept the mediation fallback; if not, flag now.

Best,
Janelle
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Janelle Peters <janelle.peters@blueridgeanalytics.com>; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai; Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueridgeanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-09-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines: carve-out for trade-secret confidentiality breaches

Janelle / Ben / Team —

Thanks — quick responses to each point below and attached a tracked redline (BRA_MSA_redlines_v3.docx updated).

1) Burden of proof: we’re fine adding an express statement that liability is subject to a preponderance of evidence standard in the forensic report.
2) Preservation window: we can agree to 120 days, provided BR documents the preservation steps in writing within 7 days of notice.
3) Equitable relief: Redwood will preserve the right to seek injunctive or other equitable relief notwithstanding the damage limitation, but we’ll limit immediate injunctive remedies to cases where the forensic snapshot indicates an ongoing exfiltration risk.

Next steps: I’ll upload the tracked-change MSA to HubSpot and push a DocuSign packet if Tom confirms procurement alignment. Ben — please confirm commercial acceptance and finalize the order form so we can close customs/finance approvals this week.

— Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BRA_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (tracked changes), evidence_protocol_summary.pdf
